messages.content: Why should teapots not be admitted into higher education?

Teapots should not be admitted into higher education because admission presupposes capacities teapots do not have: understanding, communication, independent judgment, participation in assessment, and responsibility for academic work.

That said, if “teapots” is a metaphor for unconventional applicants, then exclusion should not rest on tradition or appearance. The relevant question is whether the applicant can meet the educational requirements—not whether they resemble the usual student.

Why should teapots not be admitted into higher education?

They generally shouldn’t be admitted as students because teapots lack the agency needed to enroll, study, consent, complete assessments, or participate in academic life.

That said, a teapot could still belong in higher education—as an object of study in design, history, ceramics, engineering, or philosophy. The better rule is not “no teapots,” but “admit applicants who can meaningfully take part in the program.”
